findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 There were no paper towels available at the hand sink. Paper towels were provided during the inspection. 

Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15 Upon entrance, the hand sink was observed to be enclosed by a wheeled garbage can, an island table, and a reach-in freezer. The garbage can was moved and CK and Sam had a discussion regarding the need to keep the garbage can uncovered and moved to a location that would not make the hand sink inaccessible.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Personal foods are being stored in the upright cooler. Several opened beverage containers are observed on the various shelves. Discussed placing the personal foods on the lowest shelf of the upright cooler. 

Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1)  Observed two cartons of eggs stored in two different locations within the upright cooler. Both cartons being stored over ready-to-eat foods. The eggs were moved to the lower shelf. 


Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: The only Certified Food Protection Manager, also the only employee who handles food, isn’t performing duties as necessary. The individual isn't properly educated on ware-washing (including wash, rinse, sanitize), date marking, prevention of cross contamination, creation of sanitizer buckets, handwashing, etc. During the visit, the inspector demonstrated how to create sanitizer solutions and how to accurately test the concentration. Overall, the CFPM failed to demonstrate basic knowledge of food safety. The inspector will bring helpful handouts for the facility to use as reference for preventing the spread of food borne-illness on the follow date of 10/16/2025.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to turn off the faucet handle after washing hands. Discussed with PIC proper handwashing techniques. Ensure that employees use barriers to operate faucet handles after the handwashing process to avoid recontaminating freshly washed hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There wasn’t hand soap available at the kitchen’s handwashing sink. Discussed with PIC and soap was provided to the sink. Ensure that all hand sinks are equipped with soap to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The PIC was observed rinsing dishes in the triple sink, skipping over the wash and sanitize step. Discussed the process of wash, rinse, and sanitizing utensils and dishes before and after use to ensure that any bacteria present is reduced and safe for public consumption. The inspector will provide the facility with wash, rinse, and sanitize handouts to use for reference when ware-washing occurs. All food contact surfaces must go through the wash, rinse, and sanitize process.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: None of the TCS foods stored in house were date marked. The items contained deli meats, sliced cheeses, shredded lettuce, pizza toppings, etc. Discussed the importance for date marking and which items require date marking. Ensure that TCS foods stored in house are marked with the date of preparation and never held for longer than seven days. Will follow-up on 10/26/2025.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: A cutting board was observed stored behind the faucet handles of the triple sink. Discussed proper storage for food contact surfaces to prevent contamination and the board was moved to a different location. Ensure that food contact surfaces are stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The quaternary ammonia test strips that were available at the facility were expired and didn't have the ability to accurately test the sanitizer concentration. Discussed with PIC and a package of quat test strips were given to the facility to correct the violation. A demonstration on how to properly test sanitizer concentrations was shown to the PIC. Ensure that test strips are always valid and available to accurately test the concentration of sanitizer solutions.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer solution present while food prep was occurring. Discussed with PIC and a sanitizer solution was created and tested at 200ppm (quat). If the facility is serving food, preparing, or handling food, ensure that a sanitizer solution is always present to be sure that food contact surfaces are properly getting sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There aren’t any stoppers available to plug each compartment of the triple sink. Stoppers must be available in order for ware-washing to occur correctly. The facility can’t contain wash, rinse, or sanitize water for warewashing without stoppers. Provide stoppers for use during ware-washing. Will followup on 10/16/2025.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.12(A) Manual Warewashing, Sink Compartment Requirements. (A) Except as specified in (C) of this section, a sink with at least 3 compartments shall be provided for manually washing, rinsing, and SANITIZING EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: There is a tube that is draining contaminated water in the right compartment of the triple sink. The PIC mentioned that the tube is connected to the AC unit and water was observed draining into the sink basin. The PIC also mentioned that the tube has been draining into the sink prior to facility taking ownership. See that the tube is repaired or contained in a manner that doesn’t expose food contact surfaces to contamination. Will follow up on 10/16/2025.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: There is a leaking pipe at the top surface of the two door standing cooler. The leak is at the very top of the cooler and is tied with a glove to attempt to contain the leak. There is also an aluminum pan present to catch the leaking water. Discussed with PIC. All food intended for public consumption was moved so that they aren’t exposed to contamination. See that the leak is repaired to avoid contaminating food items stored inside of the cooler.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
An employee was observed using bare hands to turn off the faucet handle after washing hands. Discussed with PIC and violation was corrected. Ensure that employees use barriers to operate faucet handles after the handwashing process to avoid recontaminating hands. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
There wasn't any hand soap available at the kitchen hand-sink. Discussed with PIC and hand soap was provided from a shelf in the grocery store area. Ensure that hand soap is available at all times in order to wash hands properly. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed a carton of eggs to be stored above ready to eat items such as salad dressings in the kitchen prep cooler. Discussed with PIC and eggs were moved to the bottom of the cooler. Ensure that eggs are stored on the bottom shelf to prevent contaminating RTE food items. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Personal items such as but not limited to drinks and snacks were stored in the prep cooler with food items intended for public consumption. Discussed with PIC and items were removed from the cooler. Ensure that personal food or drinks are stored in a designated area away from food and drink items intended to be sold to the public. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.
